windowTitle: Serial integration regression fix - built Agent delivery refused by the mutual-exclusion guard
scope: Fix a real regression found by the Cloud Qualification fabric job (run 36644007785, TestLocalFirstApplicationDeploymentQualification): the Workspace caller presented both the explicit agent applicationSelection and the legacy top-level capabilityVersionId, which Serve refuses as mutually exclusive, so no built Agent could be delivered.
rootCause: While adding the default-App application selection union, services/workspace/internal/launch/runtime.go set both ApplicationSelection and CapabilityVersionId on the Reserve and Deploy commands, and Serve's Reserve/validateReserved treated the legacy top-level CapabilityVersionId as the agent source. Serve correctly requires exactly one source, so the built-Agent flow was refused with 'application selection and capability version are mutually exclusive'.
implemented: services/workspace/internal/launch/runtime.go: the Reserve and Deploy commands carry only ApplicationSelection; the agent's CapabilityVersion lives inside the selection (its single authoritative source).
services/serve/internal/delivery/write.go: Reserve reads the agent capability version from selection.GetCapabilityVersionId(), never from the legacy top-level field.

services/serve/internal/delivery/runtime.go: validateReserved validates the agent capability version against the explicit selection (falling back to the legacy field only when no selection was presented), so a reserved Agent row validates for both the current and a recovered legacy command shape.

services/serve/internal/delivery/write_postgres_test.go: TestServeAgentReservationFromSelectionWithoutLegacyField reserves and deploys a built Agent from the explicit selection alone and asserts the reserved row records the capability version from that selection.

commands: Cloud Qualification run 36644007785 on main HEAD f3a1c6ce reproduced the failure in the fabric job before this fix
verification.environment: local loopback PostgreSQL container; the failing job is the real Linux qualification host in the Cloud Qualification workflow
cases: Serve and Workspace modules pass with the fix; the new regression test passes.
The pre-fix failure is a real Cloud Qualification failure, not a local-only artifact.

notRun: Re-dispatch of the Cloud Qualification workflow to confirm the fabric job now passes (the fabric job needs the qualification host's privileged project-quota and Docker paths).
Candidate build, Instance deployment, production readback.
claimBoundary: This receipt claims the built-Agent delivery regression is fixed in source with focused module tests and that the failure was reproduced by a real Cloud Qualification run. It does not claim the qualification job has been re-verified green until the workflow is re-dispatched.
